title: Return of the Obra Dinn
edition_version: PC/Mac Oct 2018; Switch/PS4/Xbox One Oct 2019 (ports by Warp Digital)
key_findings: Player must determine identity, cause of death and killer for all 60 people aboard using a logbook (crew roster, drawings, ship plan) and a pocket watch that replays the moment of each death.
Answers are confirmed only in batches of three correct fates (pairs near the end), a deliberate anti-guessing mechanism later copied across the genre (e.g., The Roottrees Are Dead).
Pope added chapters and logbook structure to make a nonlinear timeline legible; he tracked characters and fates in spreadsheets.
Steam store lists Arabic interface and subtitles (no Arabic audio); base price USD 19.99; no mobile version.
Won BAFTA Game Design and Artistic Achievement 2019, IGF Seumas McNally Grand Prize 2019; critics praised the book-based interface, Game Informer criticized the ending.
Pope shifted the core puzzle from cause of death (visually easy) to identity; faces lit consistently for readability (ATH-SRC-0265, ATH-SRC-0266).
athar_applications: Adopt batch validation (confirm only when N independent conclusions are right) to make brute-forcing expensive without punishing partial progress.
Use a diegetic case notebook as the primary UI and a frozen-moment scene as an evidence container.
Precedent that an Arabic-localized deduction game exists commercially: ATHAR's differentiation cannot rest on 'first Arabic deduction game' claims without checking.
limitations: PC/console only; first-person 3D navigation does not transfer directly to phones.
Very long (60 fates); difficulty and length exceed typical 13-15 session tolerance.
Contains depictions of violent deaths; not designed for teens.

title: The Case of the Golden Idol
authors: Color Gray Games (Andrejs Kļaviņš, Ernests Kļaviņš)
edition_version: PC/Mac Oct 2022; Switch May 2023; Android/iOS via Netflix Games Jun 2024; Redux free update Oct 2024 (adds hint system)
key_findings: Each case is a single frozen moment: in Exploring mode the player clicks people, objects and documents to collect keywords; in Thinking mode the keywords fill blanks in an incomplete account of events.
Segments of the account lock when fully correct; the game signals when a segment is close (a small number of wrong words), giving partial feedback.
Shipped on Android and iOS through Netflix Games in June 2024, proving the word-slot deduction loop works on touchscreens.
The 2024 Redux update added a hint system (details not documented in the verified page).
Some reviewers criticized cases that still required trial-and-error guessing and unclear clues.
athar_applications: Core candidate loop for ATHAR: collect terms from evidence, then assemble a structured account; the account itself becomes the assessment artifact.
Validate per segment rather than whole-case to keep recoverable mistakes and avoid all-or-nothing frustration.
Netflix-bundled mobile distribution is a competitive signal: high-quality deduction games can reach phones at zero marginal price to subscribers.
limitations: Arabic not listed for the sequel on Steam; Arabic support for the original not confirmed.
Mature themes (murder, occult) and dark humor; not age-targeted.
Partial-feedback threshold can make guessing viable, as the developers themselves acknowledged (see ATH-SRC-0226).

title: The Rise of the Golden Idol
edition_version: 12 Nov 2024 PC/consoles; mobile via Netflix Nov 2024; four DLC packs in 2025
key_findings: Sequel set in the 1970s; keeps keyword collection and sentence completion, and adds overarching narrative blocks that connect scenes within and across chapters.
Steam page: USD 19.99; end-of-chapter puzzle revisits earlier deductions; reworked interface for gathering key terms from observation and testimony.
Steam lists 12 interface/subtitle languages; Arabic is not among them.
Metacritic 85; OpenCritic 92% recommend (per Wikipedia).
athar_applications: Model for season-level meta-deduction: each case contributes facts to a cross-case hypothesis.
Arabic absence in the leading deduction franchise is a localization gap relevant to ATHAR positioning.
limitations: Not educationally designed; no measurement of reasoning quality beyond correctness.
Mobile access tied to Netflix subscription.

title: Her Story
key_findings: Player types search terms into a simulated police database to retrieve short clips (271 in total) from interviews with one woman; interviews cannot be watched in full.
Search returns only the first five clips per term, so revealing clips require several related terms (confirmed in ATH-SRC-0268).
Players can tag clips with their own words, which become searchable: the player authors the index.
Barlow cited dissatisfaction with L.A. Noire and Ace Attorney interrogation models and drew on real interview records and the Serial podcast's ambiguity.
Sold over 100,000 copies by Aug 2015 (about 40,000 on iOS); won BAFTA Game Innovation and Mobile & Handheld, IGF Grand Prize.
Criticism: some players encounter major revelations early depending on search order.
athar_applications: Search-as-investigation is a native phone interaction (typing a query) and turns curiosity into the input itself.
Player-tagging of evidence is a cheap, measurable trace of hypothesis formation for assessment.
Need guardrails against early spoilers: gate critical revelations behind compound queries or prerequisite tags.
limitations: Relies on high-quality live-action performance; production cost and casting risk.
Ambiguous ending suits adults; may frustrate younger players who expect a verified solution.
Search depends on language: Arabic morphology (roots, clitics) makes keyword matching much harder than English.

title: Telling Lies
key_findings: Player searches a stolen hard drive of video clips; can highlight words in subtitles as search terms and scrub within clips.
Each clip shows only one side of a conversation, so the player must infer the missing side and match clips.
Roughly four to five times Her Story's content; three endings depending on whose videos are explored most; real-time session limit.
Critics noted an unintuitive interface (IGN) and weak felt agency due to lack of structure (GameSpot).
athar_applications: One-sided conversation is a strong inference task (reconstructing the absent speaker) adaptable to text messages or voice notes.
Warning case: scaling content 4-5x without structure reduced perceived agency; ATHAR needs scaffolds (timeline, people list) around open search.
limitations: Mature themes (surveillance, relationships); rated 17+ on iOS per App Store listing seen in search results.
Session timer that erases notes is hostile to mobile/interrupted play.

title: Unheard - Voices of Crime
edition_version: Steam 28 Mar 2019; Switch edition exists (Nintendo eShop listing)
key_findings: Investigation through sound only: the player replays recorded conversations at past crime scenes, moving between rooms to follow characters without controlling any of them.
Player matches voices to a list of known names using distinguishing traits, and answers are checked with feedback on how many are correct.
Steam price USD 6.99; languages English, Simplified/Traditional Chinese, Japanese; no Arabic.
Nonlinear: order of reconstruction is the player's choice; audio replayable without limit.
athar_applications: Audio evidence (voice notes, overheard calls) is a low-visual-cost, phone-native evidence channel; also accessibility relevant.
Voice-to-name matching is a clean, gradeable inference task with partial-correct feedback.
limitations: Spatial audio needs headphones; noisy environments degrade it.
Small commercial footprint; little public design documentation.

title: The Roottrees are Dead
publisher: Evil Trout (2025 remaster); Jeremy Johnston (2023 free original)
edition_version: Original free browser game 2023 (itch.io); commercial remaster Steam 15 Jan 2025
key_findings: Player fills a family tree (name, photo, occupation per relative) on an evidence board using photos, notes and a mock late-1990s web search engine, library site and periodical database.
Answers lock after every three correct entries, following Obra Dinn (per Thinky Games listing).
'Intuition' tab sorts evidence by number of clues it contains; a 'Notable Roottrees' list marks searchable people: built-in soft guidance.
Original used Midjourney art and was released free because Steam barred generative-AI games then; remaster replaced art with commissioned illustrations.
Metacritic 87; Game Informer 9.25/10.
athar_applications: Simulated search engine inside the case is a highly phone-compatible, scalable evidence mechanic.
Evidence sorting by 'clue density' is a non-spoiling meta-hint worth copying.
AI-art backlash is a reputational risk signal for ATHAR's AI content pipeline.
limitations: PC only; dense text and many tabs need redesign for small screens.
Built as a jam game; limited design documentation.

title: Heaven's Vault
key_findings: Player learns an invented hieroglyphic language by translating inscriptions; over 1,000 words; the narrative is nonlinear and choices affect plot.
Metacritic 76 (PC), 71 (PS4); won IGF Excellence in Narrative.
No mobile release listed.
athar_applications: Precedent for 'provisional knowledge': the player commits to tentative interpretations that can be revised as more evidence arrives, directly mapping to hypothesis revision skills.
limitations: Slow traversal criticized; mixed scores show the mechanic is niche.
Language puzzles are English-centric (see ATH-SRC-0232).

title: Outer Wilds
authors: Mobius Digital (Alex Beachum, Loan Verneau, Kelsey Beachum et al.)
edition_version: Windows/Xbox One May 2019; PS4 Oct 2019; PS5/XSX 2022; Switch Dec 2023; DLC Echoes of the Eye 2021
key_findings: 22-minute time loop; the only thing carried between loops is information recorded in the ship's computer log, organized by location or as a web of connections: knowledge is the progression.
Began as Alex Beachum's USC master's thesis (2012); won IGF Grand Prize and Excellence in Design 2015.
Level art detail is deliberately uneven to guide attention; alien texts were written as branching conversations each hinting at where related writing can be found.
Sold over 2 million copies by Aug 2021; BAFTA Best Game 2020.
Critics noted uneven difficulty and getting stuck without direction.
athar_applications: Knowledge-gated (not item-gated) progression is the cleanest mapping of 'learning = progress' and fits reasoning skills.
Auto-generated, location-or-graph case log is a template for ATHAR's evidence board.
Every clue should point to where the next clue lives (breadcrumb redundancy).
limitations: Not mobile; 3D navigation-heavy.
Getting stuck is common; ATHAR's younger players need more scaffolding than Outer Wilds offers.

title: The Forgotten City
edition_version: Skyrim mod Oct 2015; standalone Jul 2021 (PC, PS4/5, Xbox); Switch cloud Sep 2021
key_findings: A 'Golden Rule' punishes the whole city if anyone sins; the definition of sin is deliberately ambiguous and records contradict each other.
When the rule is broken, the player restarts the loop keeping items and information: failure resets the world, not the player's knowledge.
Four endings; script grew from ~35,000 to 80,000+ words between mod and standalone.
Won Australian Writers' Guild award (mod) and narrative awards; criticized for combat and backtracking.
athar_applications: Loop-with-retained-knowledge is a safe way to let teens make wrong accusations and replay with insight.
Ambiguous rules can be a teaching device for interpreting contradictory sources.
limitations: Not mobile; 3D RPG production scale.
Violence and mature moral content.

title: Pentiment
key_findings: Player collects evidence and talks to townsfolk, but time is limited so not every lead can be pursued; ends with an accusation based on belief or on who deserves punishment.
Peabody Award 2023; GDC Choice Best Narrative 2023; Metacritic 88 (PC).
Director stated the mystery was designed so there cannot be a single right answer (see ATH-SRC-0228).
athar_applications: Opportunity-cost investigation (limited actions) teaches prioritization of leads.
Counter-model for ATHAR: deliberately unresolved cases suit adult literary play but conflict with assessable reasoning; use only in advanced/ethics tracks.
limitations: Unresolved culprit makes correctness-based assessment impossible by design.
Slow pace criticized by some outlets.

title: Ace Attorney (series)
edition_version: First game GBA Japan 2001; trilogy on iOS/Android since 2012-2013
key_findings: Two-phase loop: investigation (search locations, gather evidence, interview) and trial (press testimony statements, present evidence to expose contradictions).
Mistakes drain a penalty meter (exclamation marks, later a judge's patience bar); losing it all means a guilty verdict, i.e., recoverable but bounded failure.
Psyche-Locks gate sensitive topics until the player presents the right evidence.
Series sold 15 million copies by June 2026; available on iOS/Android.
Common critiques: linearity, trial-and-error because only one specific evidence item is accepted, statements that must be pressed in a fixed order.
athar_applications: 'Present evidence against a statement' is the most proven contradiction-detection interaction and fits a phone tap-and-choose UI.
Penalty meter is a recoverable-failure pattern; ATHAR should add explanation of why a contradiction is wrong instead of just a penalty.
limitations: Single accepted answer per contradiction encourages guessing; reasoning quality isn't measured.
Japanese courtroom conventions and comedic tone don't transfer directly to Arab legal contexts.

title: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective
edition_version: DS 2010; iOS 2010/2012; HD remaster 2023 (Switch/PS4/PC/Xbox); mobile remaster 28 Mar 2024
key_findings: In a frozen 'Ghost World' the player moves between object cores; in real time they manipulate objects to change events.
Player returns to four minutes before a death to prevent it; failure rewinds to the start of the sequence, success creates a timeline checkpoint.
Mobile remaster released worldwide on Android/iOS 28 Mar 2024 (Gematsu).
Reviewers split on puzzles: linear solutions and trial-and-error frustration.
athar_applications: Rewind-to-checkpoint is a direct template for 'mistakes without ending the experience'.
Causal-chain puzzles train counterfactual and causal reasoning (what would change the outcome?).
limitations: Timing-based execution puzzles add dexterity load unrelated to reasoning.
Weak original sales (81k physical in Japan by Dec 2010).

title: Postmortem: The Painscreek Killings
title_ar: تشريح ما بعد الإطلاق: جرائم بينزكريك
edition_version: Published 2 Oct 2019; game by EQ Studios released 27 Sep 2017
key_findings: Team deliberately avoided quest markers, hints and compass overlays; the whole town opens at once and clues, not locked doors, steer the player.
Each main puzzle had several subtle hints (breadcrumbs) so players connect dots themselves rather than needing Sherlock-level leaps.
Beta testers experienced Act 2B as a passive ride (collecting keys until the killer was revealed); four months before launch it was rebuilt so every NPC was a suspect to be ruled out.
About 40,000 units sold by 2019; ~86% positive reviews; localization into nine languages drove ~35% of monthly sales.
Lessons: unfinished pre-production produced hundreds of unused assets; engine switch and late optimization hurt launch.
athar_applications: Redundant breadcrumb clues per deduction are a cheaper and more robust alternative to explicit hint UI.
Test explicitly for 'passive progression' where players advance without reasoning; redesign so elimination of suspects is player work.
Localization was a material revenue lever even for a niche detective game.
limitations: Single indie project, self-reported by a team blogger; sales figures unaudited.
Hardcore PC audience; 'no hand-holding' would likely fail with 13-15 players without fallback hints.

title: Paradise Killer
key_findings: Nonlinear open 3D investigation; trial can be started at any time, but more evidence makes convictions more effective.
Metacritic 81 (PC/Switch), 89 (PS5); praised for open-ended investigation and endgame trial; some reviewers found it slow.
Design details from developers in ATH-SRC-0227: fixed underlying truth, player may accuse anyone, game does not confirm correctness, evidence is auto-categorized.
athar_applications: 'Trial when ready' lets players choose when their case is strong enough, a direct exercise in evidence sufficiency judgment.
ATHAR should keep a fixed ground truth (like Paradise Killer) but, unlike it, give post-verdict reasoning feedback for learning.
limitations: No correctness feedback is pedagogically weak for learners.
Adult themes (cult, sacrifice) and stylized violence.

title: The Witness
key_findings: Line-drawing panel puzzles teach rules entirely through sequences of examples; no text explains rules.
Blow avoided over-tutorializing to preserve epiphanies, and made the island open so stuck players can go elsewhere rather than be blocked.
Criticism: lack of guidance makes some players 'bounce off'; unclear feedback; USD 39.99 price seen as high.
Over 100,000 copies first week; development cost just under USD 6M.
athar_applications: Teach a reasoning rule through a graded sequence of mini-cases before the real case (inductive tutorial).
Always provide parallel open problems so being stuck on one doesn't block the session.
limitations: Abstract puzzles; little narrative; high bounce-off risk for casual teens.
iOS port exists but touch line-drawing at small scale is fiddly (not verified by source).

title: The Talos Principle
edition_version: PC Dec 2014; Android May 2015; iOS Oct 2017; sequel 2023; Reawakened remaster 2025
key_findings: 120+ puzzles; players can request one-time hints from in-world 'messengers' (a scarce, diegetic hint economy).
Philosophical text terminals let the player argue with an AI interlocutor about personhood: reasoning dialogue as narrative.
Writers joined about a year into development to connect puzzles with narrative: story layered onto existing puzzles.
athar_applications: Scarce diegetic hint tokens as a pattern.
Argument-with-a-terminal dialogues as a model for Socratic critical-thinking scenes.
limitations: Spatial puzzles not detective reasoning; relevance mainly to hint economy and dialogue design.

title: Shadows of Doubt
edition_version: Early access Apr 2023; full release 26 Sep 2024 (PC, PS5, Xbox Series)
key_findings: City, citizens, routines and murders are procedurally generated per save; evidence includes fingerprints, CCTV and witness accounts.
Case closes via a resolution form: only the killer's name is required, optional fields (address, evidence, weapon) earn bonuses; wrong accusation costs a fine and the killer continues.
Mixed reception (Metacritic 68): praised for freedom; criticized for repetitive procedural cases lacking narrative connection and for bugs that made cases unsolvable.
athar_applications: Resolution form with required and optional fields is a ready model for graded case submission (core answer + supporting claims).
Evidence that procedural mysteries scale content but lose narrative quality: ATHAR should keep authored cores with procedural variation at the edges.
limitations: Mature noir content; PC/console only.
Systemic bugs can break solvability: a major risk for any generated case.

title: Detective Grimoire: Secret of the Swamp
edition_version: iOS 2 Jan 2014, then Android/PC/Mac/Linux; sequel Tangle Tower 2019 (Apple Arcade first)
key_findings: Mobile-first point-and-click murder mystery released first on iOS; sequel Tangle Tower launched on Apple Arcade.
Deductions are built by dragging elements into gaps of a sentence and rotating phrases (see ATH-SRC-0233).
Tangle Tower won IndieCade 2020 Best Performance; compared to Professor Layton.
athar_applications: Closest mobile, age-appropriate tonal reference for 13-15: gentle mystery with assembled conclusions.
Shows that heavy hinting and optional highlight mode make the game too easy for older players; ATHAR needs adjustable support.
limitations: Short; low difficulty; not designed for measurable learning.

title: Duskwood - Detective Story
edition_version: Episodic (E1-E10 per App Store version notes); visible version history starts 2020
key_findings: Story told through a messenger interface with pictures, videos, voice messages and calls; choices change how characters respond; released in episodes.
Free with in-app purchases from USD 1.99 up to USD 149.00 (credits) and packs (e.g., USD 12.99).
US App Store: 4.4 average from 2.6K ratings; age rating 13+ (realistic violence, horror/fear themes).
10 languages listed; Arabic not included.
athar_applications: Proof that a fully diegetic phone-native format (the phone is the case file) works commercially for the 13+ band.
Monetization caution: high-priced credit bundles aimed at a teen audience are a reputational and regulatory risk ATHAR should avoid.
limitations: Choices mostly relational; little verifiable deduction; no assessment of reasoning.
Download/revenue figures not verified (press sheet unavailable).

title: The Room
edition_version: iOS Sep 2012; Android 2013; Windows 2014; Switch 2018; sequels 2013-2020
key_findings: Touch gestures simulate turning keys, sliding panels and pulling levers on a 3D puzzle box; a special lens reveals hidden layers.
Sold over 6.5 million copies by Oct 2016; series over 11.5 million; Apple iPad Game of the Year 2012; BAFTA Best British Game.
Built by a small team; prototype in ~6 weeks; no characters or voice acting so mechanics carry the experience (ATH-SRC-0230).
athar_applications: Tactile evidence handling (rotate, open, reveal with a lens) is the strongest proven phone-native interaction for physical evidence.
A 'lens' mode that reveals hidden traces maps to safe forensic-light simulations (fingerprint powder, UV) without gore.
limitations: Manipulation puzzles, not inference; risk of 'puzzle box' fun displacing reasoning.

title: Escape Simulator
key_findings: Digital escape rooms modeled on real ones: take, inspect and break objects; up to 10 players online co-op.
Room Editor with 3,000+ player-made rooms; reported 2 million units by May 2022.
Reviewers credit co-op play as the main source of fun.
athar_applications: Co-op team mode and user-generated cases are proven engagement levers; a teacher room editor could serve ATHAR's school channel.
limitations: No mobile version; escape-room puzzles are often search/lock puzzles with weak reasoning content.

title: Colossal Cave Adventure
key_findings: Considered the first well-known interactive fiction and adventure game; one- or two-word typed commands via a parser.
Zork began within a month of Woods's 1977 version.
athar_applications: Historical baseline for parser interaction; modern LLM-based free text input is effectively a new parser and inherits its classic problem (guess-the-verb).
limitations: Historical; rights status unclear.

title: Sherlock Holmes: Crimes & Punishments
key_findings: Deduction board links clues into candidate conclusions; different interpretations yield different results, so the player can succeed or fail.
Each case has 3-5 possible solutions and 6-10 endings; player then chooses to absolve or condemn the culprit.
IGN criticized final deductions for relying largely on circumstantial evidence; Metacritic 71-77.
athar_applications: Deduction board where clue pairs produce intermediate conclusions is a strong mobile-adaptable pattern for chained inference.
Multiple plausible solutions train the habit of considering alternative hypotheses, but ATHAR must keep one best-supported answer for assessment.
limitations: Circumstantial-chain criticism: risk of rewarding plausible but weakly supported stories.

title: L.A. Noire
edition_version: PS3/X360 May 2011; PC Nov 2011; Switch/PS4/XOne Nov 2017
key_findings: MotionScan facial capture; for each answer the player chooses believe, doubt, or accuse; accusing requires presenting evidence that proves the lie.
Intuition points remove a wrong option or show the most popular community answer.
Reviewers found choices vague and sometimes illogical; Official Xbox Magazine criticized the passive nature of interviews.
athar_applications: Requiring evidence to support an accusation is good; reading 'lies' from facial expressions is not: it reinforces a demeaned-science myth (demeanor-based lie detection) and must be avoided in ATHAR.
Community-answer hint is a social hint pattern worth testing.
limitations: Mature content (violence, 1940s crime).
Interrogation framing conflicts with safety rule against coercive interrogation content.

title: Disco Elysium
edition_version: Windows Oct 2019; Final Cut Mar 2021; Android visual-novel version Aug 2025
key_findings: Thought Cabinet: thoughts unlocked in dialogue are 'internalized' over in-game hours into slots; completed thoughts give benefits and drawbacks; slots are limited.
24 skills speak as inner voices offering suggestions whose usefulness depends on investment.
Dice-based checks; design embraces failure with negative effects and quirks; 5M+ copies sold by Sep 2025; Android version 2025.
athar_applications: 'Hypothesis incubation' slots: a limited set of hypotheses the player commits to, each altering what they notice; maps to confirmation-bias teaching.
Failure producing new content instead of game-over is a model for recoverable mistakes.
limitations: Adult themes (drugs, politics, violence); far outside teen rating.
Dice randomness conflicts with fair, skill-based assessment.

title: Pursuing the "Aha!" moment with deductive reasoning game The Case of the Golden Idol
title_ar: السعي إلى لحظة الإدراك في لعبة قضية الصنم الذهبي
key_findings: Designers built scenarios to move players from confusion to sudden understanding and treated observed breakthroughs in playtests as the core goal.
An early free-sentence-construction mechanic was dropped; testers did better placing a limited set of phrases into blanks whose surrounding text gives grammatical and semantic context.
Whole-puzzle right/wrong grading frustrated players and invited guessing; a 'two or fewer wrong' indicator rewarded near-solutions but made the game easier and shorter (an acknowledged trade-off).
Clues were kept minimal; suspects were given similar traits so no single clue eliminates most of them; clues that trivialized a case were obscured.
Developer admits that once the designer knows the answer, judging difficulty is hard, and they had no reliable framework for mystery construction; they relied on repeated playtests.
athar_applications: Use constrained-vocabulary slots with contextual grammar instead of free-text conclusions for 13-18 users (and especially for Arabic, where free-text parsing is harder).
Partial feedback must be tuned: threshold too generous turns deduction into search; consider limiting feedback frequency or tying it to evidence citations.
Make playtest observation of 'stuck → insight' transitions a formal QA gate for every case.
limitations: Single-developer testimony, journalistic interview; no quantitative data.
Claims about testers are anecdotal.

title: How a new indie studio created one of the best detective games ever
title_ar: كيف صنع استوديو مستقل جديد إحدى أفضل ألعاب التحقيق
key_findings: No missions, markers or set paths; the player decides when to take a case to trial with whatever evidence they have.
The underlying sequence of events is fixed; the story does not bend to the player's accusation.
The game does not tell the player whether their verdict was right.

An early version required players to sort evidence into cases manually; dropped because the evidence volume made it impractical, so the game auto-categorizes evidence; the judge walks the player through each case file at trial.
Creative director framed the core principle as not pulling tricks on the player; design kept Danganronpa-style investigation but let evidence be presented at any time.
athar_applications: Manual evidence sorting at scale is a known failure; ATHAR should auto-file evidence and reserve player effort for linking and judging.
A guided 'case presentation' (judge prompts each charge) is a scaffold that structures free investigation into assessable claims.
limitations: Journalistic interview; claims not quantified.
No correctness feedback is unsuitable for learning goals.

title: Pentiment's creator intentionally designed it so 'there cannot be a right answer'
title_ar: مبتكر بنتيمنت صممها عمداً بلا إجابة صحيحة
edition_version: 8 Oct 2025 (reporting a PC Gamer interview with Josh Sawyer)
key_findings: Director Josh Sawyer decided from the start the murder mystery would have no single correct solution; some characters only seem more likely in hindsight.
Secondary report of a PC Gamer interview; the original interview was not fetched in this session.
athar_applications: Supports a separate 'open interpretation' case type for ethics/history tracks, distinct from fair-play cases used for assessment.
limitations: Secondary reporting; quote attribution relies on the outlet.

title: Pentiment - Josh Sawyer Talks Murder Mysteries
title_ar: جوش سوير يتحدث عن ألغاز القتل في بنتيمنت
key_findings: An alibi system was prototyped and cut because alibis only exclude suspects, while the team wanted evidence that rules people in.
Investigations focus on motive; means matter only for the first murder.
Players can learn who was behind the overall plot, but individual murderers are never identified beyond doubt.
athar_applications: Design choice to note: elimination (ruling out) is a core reasoning skill ATHAR wants to teach, so ATHAR should keep alibi/elimination mechanics that Pentiment cut for narrative reasons.
limitations: Tertiary summary of an interview.

title: Behind the touchscreen: The Room
key_findings: Tactility (push, twist, pull parts of the box) was treated as the game's main strength and the team iterated heavily on the control scheme.
Deliberately spartan: no characters, voice acting or big storyline so mechanics carry the experience; scoped for a very small team.
Working prototype in about six weeks; 1.4 million copies in first 11 months.
athar_applications: Prototype evidence-handling touch interactions early and cheaply; tactility is a differentiator on phones.
limitations: Commercial interview; no mention of hint system design.

title: Interview: Talking With Inkle's About Deciphering Ancient Language In Heaven's Vault
title_ar: مقابلة حول فك اللغة القديمة في قبو السماء
key_findings: The game does not say whether a translation guess is right; guesses feed into the narrative, where the protagonist theorizes about them.
Players build understanding through connections across inscriptions; designer expected players to end confident in about a third of the language, with many informed guesses.
Being wrong is part of the design; discoveries feel earned because the player reasoned to them.
athar_applications: Confidence-tagged conclusions (certain / probable / guess) let ATHAR teach calibrated belief rather than binary right/wrong.
limitations: Pre-release interview; claims may differ from shipped game.

title: Heaven's Vault (inkle)
key_findings: Translation works like a crossword: insight in one place clarifies others; very satisfying early on.
Frustration when the player understood a text but the system would not let them 'officially' read it: system knowledge lagging player knowledge.
Major choices often had little consequence while minor actions shaped the story unpredictably, producing less felt agency than actual agency.
New Game+ that keeps language knowledge makes the protagonist feel like a real expert.
athar_applications: Avoid gating on system-recognized knowledge when the player has clearly reasoned correctly: allow 'early submission' of a conclusion with evidence.
Make consequences of big choices visible to preserve felt agency.
limitations: Expert opinion (leading IF author) but a single review.

title: Detective Grimoire (SFB Games)
key_findings: Assembling a conclusion from parts (dragging elements into sentence gaps, rotating phrases) gave a stronger sense of intellectual agency than choosing from a list.
Heavy hints and a highlight mode made the game too easy; many interactions were pacing devices rather than puzzles.
Mystery-solving of this kind resembles a low-piece jigsaw: pleasure in watching the picture form, progress never really in doubt.
Core evidence-matching (e.g., a wet floor plus a missing towel) is causal reasoning that could in principle be procedurally generated from trace evidence.
Story lacked stakes and reversals; backstory existed mainly to be the solution.
athar_applications: Prefer assemble-the-claim over multiple choice for conclusions.
Rising stakes and reversals must be authored on top of the deduction loop; the solution alone is not a story.
Trace-evidence generation (event → traces → reconstruction) is a viable architecture for case variants.
limitations: Single expert review of a short game.

title: Beyond Branching: Quality-Based, Salience-Based, and Waypoint Narrative Structures
title_ar: ما بعد التفرع: البنى السردية القائمة على الصفات والبروز ونقاط العبور
key_findings: Quality-based narrative: storylets unlocked by numeric state variables (qualities); short arcs combine flexibly and avoid combinatorial branching; a murder mystery can be expressed in a handful of storylets.
Salience-based narrative: system selects the most specific applicable content for the current world state, with general fallbacks; risk of poor pacing and hard testing.
Waypoint narrative: conversation topics form a graph and NPCs pathfind toward authored beats, 'healing' the story after player detours.
All three address freedom-vs-coherence without exponential branching; Twine-like tools are poorly suited to them.
athar_applications: Model each case as storylets gated by evidence-state qualities, so players can investigate in any order while the case stays coherent.
Use salience fallbacks for NPC responses to arbitrary evidence presentation (general reply + specific replies for key evidence).
limitations: Design essay by a practitioner; no empirical evaluation.

title: Puzzle Dependency Charts
key_findings: A dependency chart is a graph of what each puzzle requires, not a flowchart of player order; designers work backward from the goal.
Charts make excessive linearity and needless choice visible at a glance.
Healthy pattern: solving one puzzle opens two or three parallel ones that converge again; games are built in acts ending in bottlenecks.
Used for nearly all Monkey Island puzzle design; Maniac Mansion's dead ends are attributed to not having them.
athar_applications: Every ATHAR case should ship with a machine-readable evidence/deduction dependency graph; it drives hint targeting, solvability checks and telemetry.
Structure cases in acts with bottleneck deductions (e.g., establish time of event) to bound freedom.
limitations: Practitioner essay; adventure-game context, not learning design.

title: Why Adventure Games Suck
key_findings: Twelve rules of thumb including: clear end goal; obvious first sub-goal; player can finish without dying if careful; no 'backwards puzzles' (problem must appear before its solution); no stranded items/dead ends.
Puzzles should advance the story; solutions should make sense in hindsight, not via trial and error; honor reasonable player intent (synonyms, proximity).
Prefer dramatic timing over strict real-time clocks; provide incremental rewards; avoid caging the player in a single locked chain.
athar_applications: Adopt as a fairness checklist for every case (especially 'problem before solution' and 'no dead ends').
'Honor player intent' becomes an NLP requirement if ATHAR accepts free text in Arabic: synonyms and dialect variants must map to the same evidence.
limitations: 1989 opinion piece; no empirical testing; some rules (no saves) are dated.

title: Return of the Obra Dinn development log (TIGSource forums)
key_findings: Player is framed as an insurance adjuster for the East India Company: a plausible institutional reason to investigate.
Pope set out to avoid the usual collect-items-and-look-for-clues structure from the first post.
Keeping 1-bit scenes legible was identified early as the hard problem; linked from Pope's official site (dukope.com).
athar_applications: Give the player a credible institutional role (e.g., youth investigator for a museum, newspaper or school) that justifies access to evidence without police/coercion framing.
Legibility of evidence is a first-order art-direction constraint, especially on small screens.
limitations: Primary but informal; long thread only partially reviewed.

title: Outer Wilds: A Thrilling Graphical Text Adventure
edition_version: Fifth-anniversary post (exact date not shown on page)
key_findings: In 2014 the director wrote a text adventure version of Outer Wilds (digitizing an earlier paper prototype) to test whether players could piece together the full mystery before building it in engine.
The text prototype was later used to onboard new staff and align the team on the game's vision; it contained the first playable ending.
athar_applications: Validate each ATHAR case as a cheap text/paper prototype (evidence cards + claim sheet) before art and engineering; measure whether testers can reach the solution unaided.
limitations: Short anniversary post; design rationale only briefly stated.

title: The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses, Third Edition
key_findings: Design quality comes from examining a game from many perspectives; the book provides over 100 sets of questions ('lenses') designers apply while building, playtesting and revising.
Third edition adds VR/AR and modern examples.
athar_applications: Use selected lenses (e.g., curiosity, problem solving, feedback) as structured review questions in ATHAR's case QA checklist.
limitations: Practitioner handbook, not empirical; lenses are heuristic and partly overlapping.

title: A Theory of Fun for Game Design
publisher: Paraglyph Press (original); O'Reilly (10th anniversary revised edition)
edition_version: Original edition ISBN 1-932111-97-2; 10th anniversary full-color revised edition (O'Reilly), foreword by Will Wright
key_findings: Official site presents the book as a meditation on why games are fun and what that says about games and people; 10th anniversary revised edition by O'Reilly.

The book's widely cited thesis (fun arises from learning and mastering patterns; boredom when no new patterns remain) was not confirmed from the fetched pages in this session and is recorded as a research interpretation.
athar_applications: If the thesis holds, each case must introduce a new pattern (reasoning move) to stay fun; repetition of the same deduction type will bore.
limitations: Publication years not confirmed in-session (left null); thesis is theoretical, not empirically tested.

title: The Art of Failure: An Essay on the Pain of Playing Video Games
title_ar: فن الإخفاق: مقالة في ألم اللعب
key_findings: Examines the paradox that people seek out games even though games regularly make them fail and feel unhappy (confirmed via author's Wikipedia entry and published reviews in Choice 2013 and Leonardo 2014).
Book frames failure as integral to the experience of games rather than an aberration; detailed typology was not retrieved in this session.
athar_applications: Design wrong accusations as informative, recoverable events rather than terminal losses; failure should produce new understanding.
limitations: Humanities essay; not an empirical study. Specific typology needs checking against the book (ISBN not confirmed in-session).

title: Twisty Little Passages: An Approach to Interactive Fiction
title_ar: ممرات صغيرة ملتوية: مقاربة للقصص التفاعلية
key_findings: Critical study treating interactive fiction as both literature and game; identifies the riddle as IF's most important literary ancestor (has a dedicated 'Riddles' chapter).
Traces the form from Adventure and Zork through Infocom to the independent IF community.
athar_applications: The riddle framing (a text that invites the reader to construct the answer) supports ATHAR's choice of constructed answers over menus.
Arabic literary tradition of riddles (ألغاز) is a potential culturally native bridge; requires check by the Arab culture team.
limitations: 2003; predates mobile and LLM-driven IF.

title: IFDB - The Interactive Fiction Database
edition_version: Live database; ~15,900 game listings at verification
key_findings: Community-built catalog managed by IFTF: ~15,916 game listings, ~17,266 reviews, ~63,138 ratings, 419 competition listings at time of check.
Supports browser play links, member lists, polls and an API.
athar_applications: Discovery source for short mystery IF to study (tag searches), and a model for community reviews of user-made cases.
API could feed a research shortlist; content license must be checked before any reuse.
limitations: Content license not stated on homepage; individual games carry their own rights.

title: Interactive Fiction Competition (IFComp)
edition_version: Annual since 1995; run by IFTF since 2016
key_findings: Judges may spend at most two hours on each game before rating; entries must be free to play.
Long-running annual event; notable winners include Photopia (1998), Lost Pig (2007), Violet (2008), The Wizard Sniffer (2017).
athar_applications: The two-hour cap is a useful benchmark: a complete, satisfying ATHAR case should fit within one to two hours, or be split into episodes.
Potential model for an Arabic youth mystery-writing competition (community content + talent pipeline).
limitations: Official site fetch failed; relied on Wikipedia for rules.

title: Universal Hint System (UHS)
edition_version: Web version since 1998; reported inactive since c. 2021 (latest hints 2015)
key_findings: Hints are organized by the specific question the player is stuck on; the player chooses how much to reveal, from subtle nudges to full answers, in contrast to walkthroughs.
Created 1988 to give hints without premature spoilers; 500+ games covered.
athar_applications: Index hints by player question ('Who could enter the room?') rather than by puzzle ID, and reveal in progressively explicit steps the player controls.
limitations: Commercial/proprietary format; no published evaluation of effect on enjoyment or learning.

title: Beyond the HUD: User Interfaces for Increased Player Immersion in FPS Games
title_ar: ما بعد شاشة المعلومات: واجهات لزيادة الانغماس
publisher: Chalmers University of Technology (Master's thesis, with EA DICE)
key_findings: Builds a UI design space based on diegesis: elements that exist in the game world and can be perceived by characters versus elements outside it (the widely cited diegetic / non-diegetic / spatial / meta taxonomy originates here; exact category wording not re-verified in this session).
Notes 'immersion' is used inconsistently and that whether HUDs harm immersion is contested.
Proposes guidelines: know the UI design space, know the game's competitive focus and fiction, establish player agency, strengthen the perceptual link between player and avatar.
athar_applications: Classify every ATHAR UI element on the diegetic axis; make the case file, phone, map and notebook diegetic objects while keeping accessibility controls non-diegetic.
limitations: FPS-focused thesis; small-sample user testing; not about mobile or learning.

title: Removing the HUD: The Impact of Non-Diegetic Game Elements and Expertise on Player Involvement
title_ar: إزالة شاشة المعلومات: أثر العناصر غير السردية والخبرة على انخراط اللاعب
key_findings: Compared two versions of a first-person shooter with and without non-diegetic HUD elements.
Removing the HUD affected immersion for expert players by increasing their sense of cognitive control; expertise moderates UI effects (per abstract via OpenAlex).
athar_applications: Do not assume removing overlay UI helps novices; test diegetic-only vs. overlay hints separately for novice and experienced players.
limitations: FPS context; sample size not in abstract; effect for novices not stated as positive.
Transfer to mobile investigation UI is an inference.

title: The Motivational Pull of Video Games: A Self-Determination Theory Approach
title_ar: الجاذبية التحفيزية لألعاب الفيديو: مقاربة نظرية تقرير الذات
key_findings: Source of the Player Experience of Need Satisfaction (PENS) approach: game enjoyment explained through satisfaction of competence, autonomy and relatedness needs, plus presence and intuitive controls (framework widely attributed to this paper; abstract not re-read in-session).
athar_applications: Measure competence and autonomy satisfaction after cases rather than 'fun' in general; autonomy is directly threatened by over-linear deduction.
limitations: Adult samples; commercial context of PENS (Immersyve) noted in literature; abstract not retrieved here.

title: Validation of two game experience scales: The Player Experience of Need Satisfaction (PENS) and Game Experience Questionnaire (GEQ)
title_ar: التحقق من مقياسين لتجربة اللعب: PENS وGEQ
key_findings: Psychometric validation study of PENS and GEQ, the two most-used player experience scales (bibliographic data verified; detailed factor results to be confirmed).
athar_applications: Before adopting PENS/GEQ items for ATHAR playtests, check which subscales held up in validation; translate and re-validate in Arabic.
limitations: Abstract not retrieved in-session.

title: Systematic Review and Validation of the Game Experience Questionnaire (GEQ) - Implications for Citation and Reporting Practice
title_ar: مراجعة منهجية والتحقق من استبيان تجربة اللعب GEQ
key_findings: GEQ has never had a formal peer-reviewed publication yet is widely used; review of 73 publications found inconsistent psychometric reporting and misleading citation practices.
Validation with 633 participants found no support for the proposed seven-factor structure of the GEQ (per abstract via OpenAlex).
Authors give recommendations for reporting and citing GEQ.
athar_applications: Do not use GEQ subscales as validated measures in ATHAR; prefer PXI items with Arabic re-validation, and report psychometrics.
limitations: Validation sample characteristics beyond size not reviewed.

title: Development and validation of the player experience inventory: A scale to measure player experiences at the level of functional and psychosocial consequences
title_ar: تطوير مقياس جرد تجربة اللاعب PXI والتحقق منه
key_findings: PXI, grounded in Means-End theory, measures functional consequences (e.g., audiovisual appeal, ease of control) and psychosocial consequences (e.g., immersion, mastery).
Items developed over two iterations with 64 games-user-research experts; validated in five studies with 529 participants.
Data supported the theorized structure, with discriminant and convergent validity and configural invariance (per abstract via OpenAlex).
athar_applications: PXI's functional layer (e.g., goals and rules clarity, progress feedback) is the most actionable instrument for diagnosing a specific case's design problems.
limitations: Full subscale list and reliability coefficients not reviewed; English adult samples; no Arabic or teen validation known.

title: GameFlow: a model for evaluating player enjoyment in games
key_findings: Condenses enjoyment heuristics into eight flow-based elements: concentration, challenge, skills, control, clear goals, feedback, immersion, social interaction, each with criteria.
Validated only by expert review of two real-time strategy games (one high-, one low-rated), where it distinguished them (per abstract via OpenAlex).
athar_applications: Use as an expert-review heuristic checklist for case drafts, not as a player-facing metric.
limitations: Weak validation (two games, expert review); a heuristic not a psychometric instrument.

title: Flow in games (and everything else)
key_findings: Designer essay (thatgamecompany) arguing for keeping players in a flow zone, with difficulty adjustment embedded in player choices rather than imposed (as commonly summarized; text not re-read in-session).
athar_applications: Offer player-chosen depth (optional sub-questions, bonus deductions) as passive difficulty adjustment instead of hidden DDA.
limitations: Short viewpoint article, not empirical.

title: Learning curves: analysing pace and challenge in four successful puzzle games
title_ar: منحنيات التعلم: تحليل الإيقاع والتحدي في أربع ألعاب ألغاز ناجحة
key_findings: Analysed play-through videos of Portal, Portal 2 (co-op), Braid and Lemmings with behavioral-psychology metrics.

Main skills are introduced one at a time, first in simple puzzles requiring only that skill, then practised and combined with earlier skills; complexity rises until the next new skill (per abstract via OpenAlex).
athar_applications: Template for auditing ATHAR's season curve: map each case to the reasoning skills it introduces vs. practises vs. combines.
limitations: Observational analysis of game design, not a player-outcome experiment; four games only.

title: Optimizing challenge in an educational game using large-scale design experiments
title_ar: تحسين مستوى التحدي في لعبة تعليمية عبر تجارب تصميم واسعة النطاق
key_findings: Two large online experiments (about 10,000 and 70,000 players) in a math game varied challenge across several design factors to test the inverted-U hypothesis.
Contrary to the hypothesis, easier versions kept players engaged longer in nearly all conditions.
The most engaging designs also produced the slowest learning; authors suggest letting players know difficulty in advance to encourage challenge seeking (per abstract via OpenAlex).
athar_applications: Run randomized variants of difficulty parameters at scale with telemetry rather than relying on designer intuition.
limitations: Single math game; online self-selected players; engagement measured as time played.
Abstract-level review only.

title: Hint systems may negatively impact performance in educational games
title_ar: قد تؤثر أنظمة التلميح سلباً في الأداء داخل الألعاب التعليمية
key_findings: Experiment with about 50,000 students in an educational game compared four hint designs modeled on hint systems that work in intelligent tutoring systems and commercial games.
All four hint designs lowered performance relative to a no-hint baseline (per abstract via OpenAlex).
Authors suggest traditional hint systems may not transfer well to educational games and call for studying player behavior.
athar_applications: Do not assume more hints = better; A/B test hint presence, timing and wording, and measure persistence and learning, not just completion.
limitations: Single educational math-type game; effect sizes and mechanisms not reviewed (abstract only).
Narrative deduction games may differ; replication in story-based contexts not found in this session.

title: Peeking Behind the Locked Door: A Survey of Escape Room Facilities
title_ar: نظرة خلف الباب المغلق: مسح لمرافق غرف الهروب
key_findings: 175 of 404 contacted facilities responded (43%); sample skewed to Europe (52%) and North America (25%); 124 facilities described 224 rooms.
Most common puzzle: searching for hidden physical objects (78% of rooms); others include team communication, light/UV, counting, noticing the obvious, assembly, math, pattern recognition, riddles.
Structures: path-based (parallel chains) 45%, sequential 37%, open 13%; many hybrids.
82% use a gamemaster to help stuck players, mostly via video monitoring (76%): human-in-the-loop hinting is the norm.
Only ~39% of rooms integrate puzzles into the narrative; author stresses no single right approach and that strong rooms spark post-game discussion.
athar_applications: Path-based parallel structure is the dominant proven pattern for group play; use for ATHAR co-op/classroom modes.
Human gamemaster hinting suggests an ATHAR 'teacher/facilitator mode' for classrooms and an AI-observer analogue for solo play.
Design for post-case discussion (debrief) as part of the experience.
limitations: Self-report survey of operators, not players; non-random sample; 2015 data from a young industry.

title: Creating Engaging Escape Rooms for the Classroom
title_ar: تصميم غرف هروب جذابة للصف الدراسي
key_findings: Practitioner article (Childhood Education 94(1), 44-49) by Scott Nicholson on designing classroom escape rooms; its abstract stresses having students engage with each other and understand the narrative behind the lessons.
athar_applications: Reference for ATHAR's school package design; check its guidance on aligning puzzles with learning goals and on debriefs.
limitations: Practitioner article rather than empirical study; only the one-sentence abstract was read (2026-10-27 gap-fill).

title: Escape education: A systematic review on escape rooms in education
title_ar: تعليم الهروب: مراجعة منهجية لغرف الهروب في التعليم
key_findings: Systematic review of educational escape rooms focusing on game design features, their relations, and alignment of outcomes with learning goals.
Educators across disciplines use time limits and teamwork for different reasons and make varied puzzle-structure choices.
Reports a gap between learners' perceived content knowledge gain and actual learning; recommends aligning game mechanics with pedagogy (per abstract via OpenAlex).
athar_applications: Never use self-reported learning ('I learned a lot') as evidence of learning; measure actual skill.
Align each puzzle mechanic to a stated learning objective.
limitations: Number of studies and evidence-quality grading not in abstract; full text not reviewed.

title: MDA: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research
title_ar: إطار الآليات والديناميكيات والجماليات في تصميم الألعاب
edition_version: Framework taught at the GDC Game Design and Tuning Workshop 2001-2004
key_findings: Splits games into mechanics (rules, data), dynamics (run-time behavior) and aesthetics (emotional responses); designers can reason from desired aesthetics down to mechanics.
Eight aesthetic categories: sensation, fantasy, narrative, challenge, fellowship, discovery, expression, submission.
athar_applications: Specify each case's target aesthetics (discovery + challenge + narrative for core cases; fellowship for co-op) and trace mechanics to them.
limitations: Conceptual framework; venue and year not printed on the fetched PDF (left null).

title: "It is always a lot of fun!": exploring dimensions of digital game experience using focus group methodology
title_ar: استكشاف أبعاد تجربة اللعب الرقمي بمنهجية مجموعات التركيز
key_findings: Qualitative focus-group study by the GEQ authors exploring dimensions of game experience; part of the groundwork commonly cited for the GEQ (relationship as reported in later literature).
athar_applications: Supports running qualitative focus groups with Arab teens before adopting any translated questionnaire.
limitations: Qualitative, small Dutch samples.

title: Between Challenge and Defeat: Repeated Player-Death and Game Enjoyment
title_ar: بين التحدي والهزيمة: تكرار موت اللاعب ومتعة اللعب
key_findings: Facial EMG during a shooter with frequent deaths: players smiled after dying (reduced frown-muscle, increased smile-muscle activity) but rated deaths negatively afterwards.
The smiling response weakened as deaths repeated; authors argue death is enjoyable only while it signals ongoing challenge and progress (per abstract via OpenAlex).
athar_applications: Repeated failure without visible progress erodes enjoyment: each failed accusation must show progress (new info) and errors at the same node should trigger support.
limitations: Violent shooter context; sample size not in abstract; physiological proxies of affect.

title: ink: inkle's scripting language for writing interactive narrative
edition_version: Open source repository; Unity integration and inkjs web port
key_findings: Open-source narrative scripting language by inkle released under the MIT license; Unity plugin and inkjs JavaScript port for web.
athar_applications: Candidate authoring layer for ATHAR dialogue and storylets (web/mobile via inkjs); MIT permits commercial use with attribution; Arabic RTL rendering must be tested by the technical team.
limitations: Branching-first language; quality-based/storylet patterns require extra architecture.

title: The Case of the Golden Idol used frequent testing to sharpen its mystery-solving
title_ar: كيف استخدمت قضية الصنم الذهبي الاختبار المتكرر لصقل حل الألغاز
key_findings: Puzzles were tested as early as possible with rough prototypes (basic visuals, spreadsheets) and placeholder art; each scenario tested with a small regular group of four to five people.
Feedback came from observation and interviews rather than quantitative data.
A player who understood the main mystery but stayed stuck about thirty minutes on a technicality signaled a design problem; clues that let players skip many steps were removed.
Testers found scenarios harder when played in isolation without earlier context; pacing described as the main and easily broken concern.
athar_applications: Adopt 'understood the mystery but stuck on a technicality for N minutes' as a red-flag test metric and telemetry rule.
Remove shortcut clues that bypass intended reasoning steps; test scenarios in sequence, not only in isolation.
limitations: Developer testimony; no quantitative data; small friend-and-publisher tester pool.

title_ar: بالنسبة إلى لوكاس بوب، كانت أوبرا دين مجموعة مشكلات تصميمية جذابة
title: For Lucas Pope, Return of the Obra Dinn was a bunch of appealing design problems
key_findings: Pope first built the game around how people died, but found causes of death were usually easy to see; the interesting puzzle was who each person was (identity deduction).
The late shift to identity forced a chapter structure around disasters with an unbroken chain of deaths, presented as a book.
He describes the core mechanic as a simple, rigid matrix of features to fill for each identity.
Scaling from a four-character 2014 demo to 60 characters broke prototype tools and added roughly a year of work.
athar_applications: Put the hard reasoning in identity/relationship inference, not in what is visually obvious (e.g., cause of an event).
Plan authoring tools for full case scale from the start; demo tooling will not scale.
limitations: Interview; no data on player behavior; does not discuss validation rationale.

title_ar: لوكاس بوب وتحدي جمالية البت الواحد في أوبرا دين
title: Lucas Pope on the challenge of creating Obra Dinn's 1-bit aesthetic
key_findings: Pope spent months ensuring players could tell what they were seeing in each 1-bit scene; the style took far longer than the expected six months.
Full-screen dithering made playtesters feel ill; he warped the dither pattern with camera movement ('smooth' mode) while keeping a 'sharp' mode.
Because players cared more about who victims were than how they died, faces became central and are lit consistently so they stay readable.
Sparse style hides detail, suited a small team, and leaves gaps for players to fill.
athar_applications: Every face/identity cue in ATHAR art must be readable at phone size under all scene conditions; legibility testing is a release gate.
Choose an art style that is cheap to produce and leaves interpretive room, but never obscures required evidence.
limitations: Journalistic interview; PC context.

title_ar: إثارة الاستكشاف المدفوع بالفضول عبر السرد في Outer Wilds
title: Sparking Curiosity-Driven Exploration Through Narrative in 'Outer Wilds'
publisher: GDC (Independent Games Summit 2021; uploaded by GDC Festival of Gaming)
key_findings: GDC Independent Games Summit session by the game's writer/narrative designer on how narrative supports the core goal of curiosity-driven exploration and on specific narrative design decisions (per official video metadata; talk content not transcribed in this session).
athar_applications: Primary talk to review when designing ATHAR's clue-writing guidelines (texts that point to other texts).
limitations: Only metadata verified; content not reviewed in-session.

edition_version: 13 Oct 2015 (date per Wikipedia reference list; page shows no date)
title: Howdunnit: The making of Her Story
authors: Pocket Gamer.biz (contributing writer Kirk; byline not explicit)
key_findings: Barlow built Her Story iOS-first; adapting a mouse-driven simulated desktop to touch led him to limit the interface to single taps.
The database shows only the first five clips for any search word, holding back revealing clips until players have found several related words: a structural spoiler guard.
He used data analysis to find overused, underused, too-easy or too-hard clips and rebalanced content.
Over 100,000 copies sold; about 40% of buyers on mobile; listed prices USD 5 (iOS) and USD 6 (PC).
athar_applications: Cap result counts per query (e.g., top 3-5) so critical fragments require converging queries: direct spoiler-control technique for ATHAR archives.
Use telemetry on evidence views to rebalance over-/under-used evidence after pilot.
Single-tap interaction model for any simulated desktop/phone UI.
limitations: Trade-press interview; byline and date not explicit on page.

title: Making 'Her Story' - Telling a Story Using The Player's Imagination
title_ar: صناعة Her Story: رواية القصة بخيال اللاعب
publisher: GDC Vault (Game Developers Conference 2016, Game Narrative Summit)
key_findings: Official GDC Vault session page confirms a GDC 2016 Game Narrative Summit talk by Sam Barlow (listed as Independent) on the conception and development of Her Story.
Session summary frames the talk around writing for the player's imagination as the engine of interactive storytelling.

An attendee report (Emily Short, 16 Mar 2016) notes the talk showed a spreadsheet tracking word use to tune which search terms surface which clips; this detail is second-hand, not from the talk itself.
athar_applications: Supports treating the archive's vocabulary as a designed system: audit which player search terms reach which evidence items before release (word-use matrix in the case editor).
Primary talk to review before finalising ATHAR's free-search archive mechanic.
limitations: Talk video not viewed this session (GDC Vault was in maintenance for direct fetch; page read via fetch tool); only session metadata and summary verified.
Free/members-only status of the recording not confirmed.

title: GDC Live Q&A: Lucas Pope and Return of the Obra Dinn
title_ar: جلسة GDC المباشرة: لوكاس بوب وReturn of the Obra Dinn
publisher: GDC (official YouTube channel, 'GDC Festival of Gaming'; originally streamed on Twitch)
key_findings: Official GDC channel hosts an hour-long live Q&A with Lucas Pope about the development of Return of the Obra Dinn (published 9 Nov 2018).
This is a live Q&A, not a formal GDC conference talk; no formal GDC talk by Pope on Obra Dinn was found on the GDC channel or Vault in this round.
athar_applications: Secondary listening source for Pope's design reasoning; written interviews ATH-SRC-0265/0266 remain the citable sources for specific claims.
limitations: Video content not transcribed or reviewed in-session; only official metadata verified. Do not cite for specific design claims.

title: How The Case of the Golden Idol developers made one of the decade's best detective games, twice
title_ar: كيف صنع مطورو The Case of the Golden Idol إحدى أفضل ألعاب التحقيق في العقد مرتين
key_findings: Developers state the aim is games where the player makes the deductions rather than role-plays a detective; Obra Dinn, Her Story and Outer Wilds named as inspirations.
Built one scenario at a time (about one to two months each); prototyped and tested a single scenario before committing to the rest; large playtester pool.

DLC work exposed a complexity ceiling beyond which puzzles stopped being fun; the sequel replaced the fixed multi-panel 'thinking' screen with pop-ups added only when needed, and the word bank now auto-sorts words into names, nouns and verbs.
Every scene keyed to a dead body became limiting; the sequel centres theft, intrigue or accidents, with murder rarer.
athar_applications: Supports ATHAR's single-case vertical-slice validation before season production.
Cap per-case complexity and let the answer template grow only as needed (no fixed empty slots).
Auto-categorised word bank is a direct precedent for Arabic slot answers (names/nouns/verbs), with gender-number agreement to be checked.
Non-lethal case premises are viable for the 13-15 band and avoid repetitiveness.
limitations: Journalistic feature based on developer testimony; no data. No GDC talk by Color Gray Games was located in this round.
Article does not cover hint/fairness policy or the Netflix mobile adaptation.
